Frances Burney.bio: Novelist and diarist. Author of Evelina, Cecilia, Camilla, The Wanderer. Keeper of the Robes to Queen Charlotte 1786-91. Married Alexandre d'Arblay 1793.

Charles Burney Sr.bio: Musicologist, organist, Fellow of the Royal Society. Author of A General History of Music. Father of Frances Burney.

Charles Burney Jr.bio: Classical scholar, schoolmaster, DD. Son of Charles Burney Sr. Greek scholar at Cambridge.

Susanna Burney Phillips.bio: Frances Burney's favourite sister. Married Captain Molesworth Phillips 1782. Died in Ireland.

Esther Burney.bio: Eldest Burney daughter. Married her cousin Charles Rousseau Burney.

Charlotte Broome.bio: Burney sister. Married (1) Clement Francis 1786, (2) Ralph Broome 1798. Mother of Charlotte Barrett.

Charlotte Barrett.bio: Frances Burney's niece. Edited and published the first edition of the Diary and Letters (1842-46).

James Burney.bio: Rear-Admiral. Sailed with Captain Cook on second and third voyages. Author of Chronological History of Voyages.

Alexandre d'Arblay.bio: French artillery officer, émigré. Married Frances Burney 1793. Served under Lafayette, then Napoleon.

Alexander d'Arblay.bio: Son of Frances Burney and Alexandre. Cambridge student. Ordained 1818.

Charles Parr Burney.bio: Son of Charles Burney Jr. Clergyman, Archdeacon of Colchester. Bought books at his grandfather's auction.

Sarah Harriet Burney.bio: Half-sister of Frances. Novelist in her own right.

Maria Allen Rishton.bio: Step-sister. Daughter of Elizabeth Allen (Charles Burney's second wife). Prolific early correspondent of Frances.

Samuel Johnson.bio: Lexicographer, essayist, poet. Author of the Dictionary. Central figure of London literary life.

Hester Thrale Piozzi.bio: Writer, salon hostess at Streatham Park. Married (1) Henry Thrale, (2) Gabriel Piozzi 1784. 'Once dearest friend' of Frances Burney.

James Boswell.bio: Biographer of Johnson. Author of the Life of Samuel Johnson (1791).

Joshua Reynolds.bio: Portrait painter, first President of the Royal Academy. Founding member of The Club with Johnson.

Henry Thrale.bio: Brewer, MP for Southwark. Husband of Hester. Host of the Streatham Park literary circle.

Hester Maria Thrale (Lady Keith).bio: Eldest Thrale daughter ('Queeney'). Married Admiral Viscount Keith 1808. Sided against her mother over the Piozzi marriage.

Susanna Arabella Thrale.bio: Fourth surviving Thrale daughter. Unmarried. Died in Kent, buried at Streatham.

Sophia Thrale Hoare.bio: Third surviving Thrale daughter. Married Henry Merrik Hoare.

Penelope Pennington.bio: Piozzi's closest female friend. 164 letters in our data. Also appears in Mary Hays's biographical index (radical feminist circle).

Samuel Crisp.bio: Frances Burney's 'Daddy Crisp'. Lived at Chessington Hall, Surrey. Failed dramatist, beloved mentor.

David Garrick.bio: Actor-manager, Drury Lane Theatre. Furnished Burney with letters of introduction for the 1770 Italian tour.

Georgiana Waddington.bio: Née Port. Granddaughter of Mary Delany. Correspondent of Frances from Wales.

Frederica Locke.bio: Of Norbury Park, Mickleham, Surrey. One of Frances Burney's closest friends.

Edmund Burke.bio: Statesman, philosopher. Author of Reflections on the Revolution in France. Led the Hastings impeachment.

Horace Walpole.bio: 4th Earl of Orford. Author, antiquarian, founder of Strawberry Hill. Son of PM Robert Walpole.

William Windham.bio: Politician, Secretary at War. Connected to both Burke and the Burney circle.

Frances Crewe.bio: Née Greville. Whig political hostess. Bridge between Burke's political world and Burney's literary one.

Queen Charlotte.bio: Queen consort of George III. Frances Burney served as her Keeper of the Robes 1786-91.

Princess Sophia.bio: Daughter of George III. 181 letters with Frances Burney — an intense late friendship.

Princess Elizabeth.bio: Daughter of George III. Married Landgrave of Hesse-Homburg 1818.

Princess Mary.bio: Daughter of George III. Married Duke of Gloucester 1816.

Padre Martini.bio: Giovanni Battista Martini. Franciscan friar, music theorist at Bologna. Taught the young Mozart. Burney's key Italian Catholic contact.

Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart.bio: Composer. Burney met the 14-year-old Mozart in Bologna, August 1770.

Leopold Mozart.bio: Musician, father of Wolfgang. Met Burney in Bologna 1770.

Johann Christian Bach.bio: The 'London Bach'. J.S. Bach's youngest son. 33 letters with Padre Martini. Lived in London from 1762.

Carl Philipp Emanuel Bach.bio: J.S. Bach's second son. Keyboard virtuoso at Hamburg. Burney spent 'many happy hours' with him, October 1772.

Christoph Willibald Gluck.bio: Opera reformer. Met Burney in Vienna 1772.

Pietro Metastasio.bio: Imperial court poet and librettist in Vienna. Met Burney 1772.

Carlo Broschi Farinelli.bio: Most famous castrato of the century. Retired to Bologna. Met Burney August 1770.

Baldassare Galuppi.bio: Venetian opera and keyboard composer. 'Had more influence on English music than any other Italian composer.' Met Burney 1770.

Giovanni Battista Sammartini.bio: Milanese symphonist, pioneer of the classical style. Met Burney July 1770.

Laura Bassi.bio: First woman to hold a university chair in Europe. Professor of physics at University of Bologna. Met Burney August 1770.

Voltaire.bio: Philosopher, writer. Burney visited him at Ferney, June 1770.

Denis Diderot.bio: Philosopher, editor of the Encyclopédie. 8 letters with Burney.

Baron d'Holbach.bio: Philosopher, salon host. His salon on rue Royale Saint-Roch was 'the Cafe d'Europe'.

Jean-Jacques Rousseau.bio: Philosopher. Burney met him in Paris on the return visit, December 1770.

Madame de Stael.bio: Germaine de Stael. Writer, salon hostess. Part of the Juniper Hall émigré circle near the d'Arblays.

Jacques-Pierre Brissot.bio: Future Girondin revolutionary leader. 4 letters with Burney in the Fonds Brissot. Guillotined.

Marie de Maisonneuve.bio: French correspondent. 172 letters with Frances Burney — major post-1802 connection.

Thomas Twining.bio: Theologian, musician, rector of Fordham, Essex. Charles Burney's closest intellectual friend. 319 letters.

William Bewley.bio: Apothecary at Great Massingham, Norfolk. Burney's trusted literary advisor. Met at King's Lynn.

Thomas Gray.bio: Poet, author of 'Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard'. Had recommended the idea of a music history to Burney. Walpole's closest correspondent.

Frederick the Great.bio: King of Prussia. Flautist and composer. Burney attended his court at Potsdam, heard him perform, October 1772.

Sir William Hamilton.bio: British envoy to Naples. Antiquarian, volcanologist. Helped Burney access Royal Museum at Portici and arranged musical introductions. Later famous for wife Emma and Nelson affair.

Joseph Priestley.bio: Chemist, theologian, Dissenter. Lunar Society member. Broke with Burke over the French Revolution.

Fulke Greville.bio: Met Burney at King's Lynn. Instrumental in bringing him back to London.

Dr. Brocklesby.bio: Richard Brocklesby. Physician. Attended Samuel Johnson in his final illness. Also physician to Edmund Burke. Fellow of the Royal Society. Bridge between Johnson and Burke networks.

Abbé Arnaud.bio: Former director of the Opéra Comique, Paris. Met Burney June 1770.

Jean Monet.bio: Connected to Paris theatre world. Met Burney 1770.

William Herschel.bio: Astronomer, discovered Uranus. Musical connection to Burney — both musicians turned scientists.

William Mason.bio: Poet, garden designer. Burney wrote to him before the 1770 tour. Also Walpole correspondent.

George Montagu.bio: Walpole's most prolific correspondent (252 letters in our data).

Henry Seymour Conway.bio: Soldier, politician. Walpole's cousin and major correspondent (139 letters).

William Cole.bio: Antiquary, clergyman. Walpole's second most frequent correspondent (161 letters).

Lord Stormont.bio: David Murray, 7th Viscount Stormont. British ambassador to Austria. Facilitated Burney's introductions in Vienna 1772.

Louis Devisme.bio: British plenipotentiary in Munich. 'Of the greatest assistance' to Burney, esp. accessing the Elector's library.

John Osborn.bio: British Envoy at Dresden. Introduced Burney to the Elector.

Gaetano Guadagni.bio: Famous castrato. Created the role of Orfeo for Gluck. Met Burney in Munich 1772.

Regina Mingotti.bio: Retired opera singer. Met Burney in Munich 1772.

Nicola Jommelli.bio: Opera composer. Met Burney in Naples 1770. Catholic.

Niccolo Piccinni.bio: Opera composer, later embroiled in the Gluck-Piccinni war in Paris. Met Burney in Naples 1770.

Giovanni Paisiello.bio: Neapolitan opera composer. Active when Burney visited Naples 1770.

Gaetano Caffarelli.bio: Celebrated castrato. Retired to Naples. Met Burney 1770.

Pietro Nardini.bio: Violinist, pupil of Tartini. Met Burney in Florence 1770.

Antonio Sacchini.bio: Opera composer. Met Burney in Venice 1770, later in London.

Andre Gretry.bio: Belgian-born opera composer based in Paris. Met Burney 1770.

Claude Balbastre.bio: Organist at Saint-Roch, Paris. Burney heard him play June 12 1770 and visited his house.

Christian Cannabich.bio: Kapellmeister of the Mannheim orchestra. Met Burney August 1772.

Friedrich Klopstock.bio: Poet. Burney met him in Hamburg, October 1772.

Christoph Daniel Ebeling.bio: German musicologist, Hamburg. Translated Burney's France/Italy volume into German. Corresponded from August 1771.

Richard Shackleton.bio: Quaker schoolmaster. Burke's closest childhood friend. 21 letters with Burke.

Richard Champion.bio: Bristol porcelain manufacturer. Burke's political ally. 35 letters.

Marquis of Rockingham.bio: Charles Watson-Wentworth. Whig PM 1765-66, 1782. Burke's political patron. 49 letters.

Charles James Fox.bio: Whig politician. Burke's ally then opponent over the French Revolution.
